fact: At the All My.T Summit, ICT Minister Ramtohul highlighted forthcoming amendments to the Data Protection Act to enhance cybersecurity, protect privacy and reinforce online safety, particularly for children.

Government Notice No. 117 of 2026, the Data Protection (Designation, Tasks and Position of Data Protection Officers) Regulations 2026, was made by the Minister under section 55 of the Data Protection Act on 17 June 2026, to come into operation on 1 January 2027.

The regulations were made after consultation with the Data Protection Commissioner, and give the Office (Data Protection Office) roles in receiving DPO notifications within 14 days, certifying DPOs and approving training institutions.

New DPO regulations were made on 17 June 2026 requiring every controller to designate a data protection officer, with non-compliance an offence liable to a fine up to 100,000 rupees and imprisonment up to 5 years.

L'Express reports the Cabinet approved the Data Protection (Designation, Tasks and Position of Data Protection Officers) Regulations 2026 under the Data Protection Act 2017, with a six-month compliance period and entry into force on 1 January 2027.
Commissioner Madhub says Mauritius adopted a new data protection regime in 2017, after a first law in 2004 partly implemented in 2009, and describes it as the country's current law.
Drudeisha Madhub is named as the Data Protection Commissioner of Mauritius.
Madhub says the office can register controllers and processors, make them fill in forms, and do some enquiries and fine them, giving no count or named decision.
Madhub says that in 2026 Mauritius is going for the EU adequacy assessment and fully aligning its law with EU-GDPR requirements.

Commissioner Madhub said her office issues 3,000 enforcement actions a year, 99 percent of them resolved through amicable dispute resolution without prosecution; no year is given for the count, so the article's published date is used.

fact: The Data Protection Office has been operational since 16 February 2009 and enforces the Data Protection Act 2017; the report is signed by Data Protection Commissioner Drudeisha Madhub, who describes herself as the data protection regulator.

The Data Protection Office reports on its enforcement in 2024 of the Data Protection Act 2017, citing its sections on complaints, transfers, registration, certification and appeals; the report is dated 2024 by year only.

A draft Data Protection Bill, as recommended by the European Commission to amend the Data Protection Act for EU adequacy, was submitted by the Data Protection Office to the Ministry of Information Technology, Communication and Innovation for consideration; the report gives no date beyond 2024.

Registration of controllers and processors is carried out under the Data Protection (Fees) Regulations 2020; the report says registrations since 01 August 2020 reached 21,219 controllers and 1,157 processors by 31 December 2024.

The Data Protection Office reports for January to December 2024: 179 new complaints (158 on CCTV), 39 complaints closed, 105 personal data breaches notified, 112 cross-border transfers authorised and 12 rejected under section 36, 10 impact assessments received, and four compliance inspections.

In 2024 the Data Protection Commissioner issued guidelines for the insurance sector requiring insurance salespersons to register as processors, and made recommendations on CCTV cameras in schools after a survey; 3,076 registration certificates were issued in 2024.
The Ministry of ICT's sovereign cloud RFI requires the cloud to abide by the Data Protection Act (named as Data Protection Act 2017).
